title: Economy, Globalization, and Supply Chains
summary: Global production, supply chains, trade dependencies, labor standards, and economic resilience.
whyItMatters: Global supply chains connect prices and availability to transport, labor conditions, regulation, geopolitics, and environmental costs.

mentalModel.title: Map value, risk, and power
mentalModel.content: Follow where value is created, where disruption can occur, and which actors can shape conditions.

mentalModel.title: Efficiency and resilience differ
mentalModel.content: The cheapest system under normal conditions may be vulnerable when transport, energy, or suppliers fail.

ruleBlocks.title: Trace the supply chain
ruleBlocks.content: Distinguish raw materials, intermediate goods, assembly, logistics, retail, and after-sales services.

ruleBlocks.title: Identify dependencies
ruleBlocks.content: Examine concentration among suppliers, transport routes, critical inputs, and regulatory environments.

ruleBlocks.title: Evaluate standards and costs
ruleBlocks.content: Compare price, reliability, labor rights, emissions, transparency, and enforceability.

tables.title: Supply Chain Risk Map
rows: Can origin and conditions be verified?
Who receives value and who bears risk?

examples.de: Die Produktion ist effizient, hängt jedoch von wenigen spezialisierten Zulieferern ab.
examples.en: Production is efficient but depends on a small number of specialized suppliers.

examples.de: Höhere Standards können Kosten erhöhen und zugleich langfristige Risiken senken.
examples.en: Higher standards can raise costs while reducing long-term risks.

examples.de: Eine regionale Beschaffung ist nicht automatisch ökologischer, wenn die Produktion besonders energieintensiv ist.
examples.en: Regional sourcing is not automatically greener if production is especially energy-intensive.

commonMistakes.wrong: Equate globalization only with international trade.
commonMistakes.correct: Include finance, knowledge, labor, regulation, and production networks.

commonMistakes.wrong: Judge a supply chain by price alone.
commonMistakes.correct: Include reliability, standards, external costs, and strategic dependency.
commonMistakes.reason: Low prices can conceal transferred risks.

comparisons.summary: Formal economic analysis frequently uses established noun-verb combinations.
Supply-chain interests become concrete in negotiated price, quality, delivery, and compliance terms.
